items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Tracy Van Kalsbeek, Executive Director of KW Oktoberfest
notes:
Tracy Van Kalsbeek, Chef D (Darryl Fletcher), and Allen Cayenne, Oktoberfest appeared before the Committee regarding the decrease in Cultural Drivers of Tourism program funding for K-W Oktoberfest.

In response to a question from the Committee on the prioritization of police security and the cost of policing, A. Cayenne emphasized the importance of safety and security at the festival. He noted the challenges created by global events and the rising costs of safety measures, including barriers and other security requirements. He stated that organizers are working closely with Waterloo Regional Police Services (WRPS) and are looking for ways to reduce other costs in order to maintain their focus on public safety.

In response to a further question on the social value of the festival, A. Cayenne highlighted the community impact of K-W Oktoberfest, including the use of the festival platform to support local initiatives, partnerships that strengthen cultural ties, and the importance of fundraising for community benefit.

In response to a question on the Municipal Accommodation Tax (MAT) reserve, Rod Regier, Commissioner Planning, Development & Legislative Services responded that following this year’s Cultural Drivers of Tourism allocations, the balance is approximately $400,000. Two significant requests are anticipated in the near term, which would substantially draw down the fund. He noted the financial implications of either amending the program criteria to give special consideration to Oktoberfest or increasing the overall funding envelope to support all applicants.

B. Vrbanovic brought forward a motion. Chair M. Harris sought consent to waive notice, which was unanimously granted.

The Committee deliberated on the motion, including discussion of a potential policy change and requests for further clarification regarding the MAT reserve.

The Committee discussed the request in the context of sustainable funding and the need for a broader policy approach. M. Goetzke, Acting Chief Administrative Officer, emphasized that part of this approach involves balancing the allocation of MAT revenue between annual festivals and maintaining a reserve for one-time large events. He advised that staff will bring back recommendations on an appropriate reserve level to ensure capacity to support major events. The Ontario Summer Games is anticipated to submit a request next year, at which time Council will be able to provide specific direction.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
COR-CFN-25-013, 2025 Mid-Year Report
notes:
Connie. MacDonald, Commissioner, Resident Experience, Strategy and Communications, and Wayne. Steffler, Commissioner, Corporate Services and Chief Financial Officer, spoke to the report and provided a presentation on the 2025 Annual Business Plan Mid-Year Update. The presentation highlighted that the Strategic Plan serves as the Region’s four-year roadmap to support growth to a community of one million, with accountability and transparency to Council and the community as key priorities. Over the second quarter of 2025, the Region has worked collaboratively and efficiently to achieve results and positive outcomes in each strategic priority area. There are no major risks identified to the achievement of Annual Business Plan objectives; however, the organization continues to experience and proactively manage fiscal and service pressures related to growth, federal and provincial policy shifts, and global economic uncertainty.

In response to a Committee question regarding whether the Update includes ION Stage 2 and the proposed hospital donation, W. Steffler confirmed that it does not.
